recent_posts.title: Expert Takes on Choosing the Right Java Tools
recent_posts.summary: Java development teams face productivity challenges including insufficient documentation, communication issues, and long redeploy times. Developer experience can be quantified using frameworks like DORA, SPACE, and Core 4 metrics. Key strategies for improving productivity include investing in enterprise-ready Java tools, involving developers in tool evaluation, ensuring proper onboarding and adoption, and measuring ROI through multiple metrics rather than focusing on single measures.

recent_posts.title: 5 Tips for Investigating and Implementing Java Tools
recent_posts.summary: Modern enterprise Java development environments face complexities that hinder innovation. Investing in the right Java tools is key to enhancing productivity without adding additional developer headcount. Purpose-built tools like JRebel and GitHub CoPilot provide robust solutions, supporting effective workflows and automation. Implementing tools effectively involves empowering developers with flexible choices, making developer experience a priority, and tracking the ROI of tools used.

recent_posts.title: Enterprise Java Development Environments
recent_posts.summary: Enterprise Java development environments are increasingly complex due to the use of remote and cloud-based environments, microservices, and multiple IDEs. Focusing on improving developer experience and investing in the right development tools can help businesses overcome these challenges and accelerate time to market.

recent_posts.title: Top Java Development Tools and Software
recent_posts.summary: Java developers rely on a variety of tools to enhance their productivity. The most popular Java IDEs in 2025 are IntelliJ IDEA, VS Code, and Eclipse. IntelliJ IDEA is favored for its extensive features despite its pricing. VS Code has gained popularity for its lightweight and free nature, serving as a secondary IDE for many developers. Eclipse remains in use due to its customizability and free access. Among application servers, Apache Tomcat leads in use, followed by Jetty and JBoss/WildFly. These tools collectively address various Java development needs, making the process more efficient.

recent_posts.title: Highlights From the 2025 Java Developer Productivity Report
recent_posts.summary: The 2025 Java Developer Productivity Report highlights the increasing importance of investing in Java tools despite economic challenges. AI tools are becoming essential for tasks such as code completion and debugging. However, remote development environments present redeploy time challenges. The report is based on a survey of 731 Java professionals, including developers and business leaders.

recent_posts.title: What's New With Java 24
recent_posts.summary: Java 24, a short-term JDK release scheduled for March 2025, will introduce 24 new features, including experimental, incubator, preview, and permanent JEPs. Key highlights include the Generational Shenendoah garbage collector and compact object headers. Java 24 will be replaced by long-term support Java 25 in September 2025.

recent_posts.title: What is Developer Experience
recent_posts.summary: Happier developers are more productive, which significantly benefits a business. Developer experience (DX) focuses on reducing friction in developers' workflows and improving their job satisfaction. Key areas to improve DX include allowing choice in development tools, minimizing meetings, and automating tedious tasks. Overcoming productivity obstacles like excessive tasks and long redeploy times can also enhance DX. Improving DX can boost morale, retention, and attract new talent.

recent_posts.title: Java Documentation
recent_posts.summary: Java documentation, while essential, can be challenging to write. This post provides tips on creating effective JavaDocs, highlights the importance of documenting code clearly for team collaboration, and introduces JavaDoc best practices including the use of tags like @link, @code, and @since. It also covers tools and AI extensions that can aid in generating JavaDocs, emphasizing the value of well-documented code for maintaining readability and efficiency in Java development.

recent_posts.title: JRebel Updates in 2024
recent_posts.summary: In 2024, Java continues to be a vital component of enterprise business applications with updates including JRebel for Cloud and integrations with various IDEs like IntelliJ, Eclipse, and VSCode. JRebel has also focused on supporting a wide range of application servers, with significant updates to improve development efficiency. These updates reflect JRebel's commitment to help Java development teams save time and accelerate their processes.

recent_posts.title: What's Coming With Jakarta EE 11?
recent_posts.summary: Jakarta EE, formerly known as J2EE and Java EE, is a flexible Java framework maintained by the Eclipse Foundation. The upcoming Jakarta EE 11 will require Java SE 17 as its minimum runtime and includes updates like Jakarta Data and Jakarta NoSQL, with its release expected in late 2024 due to ongoing development and review.
